faq.q: What muscle makes hair stand up?
faq.a: The arrector pili, a tiny muscle attached to each hair follicle. When it contracts it pulls the hair upright and makes a bump in the skin.
asks: Tell me about the hair muscle

faq.q: Why do we get goosebumps when scared?
faq.a: Fear switches on the fight-or-flight system. Its nerves, and the hormone adrenaline, make the hair muscles contract, so goosebumps can come from fear as well as cold.
Hardly. In furry animals, raised fur traps a thicker blanket of air, but human body hair is too thin for that. Goosebumps are mainly a reflex left from our ancestors.

faq.q: Why can music give you goosebumps?
faq.a: Strong emotions, like being moved by music, can trigger the same nervous system pathway that causes goosebumps in the cold, so the hair muscles contract.
asks: Why do I get chills from a song?

faq.a: Because the bumpy skin looks like the skin of a plucked goose or other bird, where the feathers grew.
asks: Where does the word goosebumps come from?

facts: Each arrector pili muscle is attached to a hair follicle and contracts involuntarily.
Goosebumps are controlled by the sympathetic, or fight-or-flight, nervous system.
